notes: A. James Clark School of Engineering official Fall 2026 Materials Science and Engineering graduation plan. General-education slots (ENGL101, Oral Communication, Professional Writing, Scholarship in Practice, Humanities, History/Social Sciences) are left out: only the program's own requirements are audited here (they're covered by gen-ed-2026-27.ts).
The chemistry lecture sequence (Year 1 Fall) is filled with CHEM135 (the plan's own scheduled course), not the CHEM131/CHEM134 alternate.
The 'CHEM231 & CHEM232 or CHEM481' slot (Year 2 Spring) is filled with CHEM231 and CHEM232, as printed first on the graduation plan; CHEM481 alone would satisfy the requirement equally.
The 'ENES200 or ENEE200' slot (Year 2 Fall) is filled with ENES200, as printed on the graduation plan and catalog table; ENEE200 would satisfy the requirement equally.

The two 'ENMA312 OR Upper Level Science Elective' slots (Year 3 Fall and Spring) are filled with ENMA312 (Year 3 Fall, the specific required course) and CHEM425 (Year 3 Spring, an illustrative upper-level science elective -- no enumerable list of eligible courses exists per source, so this slot isn't audited as a program requirement; any qualifying upper-level science course would do).

The five 'Specialization Elective' slots (Year 3 Fall/Spring, Year 4 Fall, Year 4 Spring x2) are filled with ENMA410, ENMA421, ENMA422, ENMA426 and ENMA481, all from the department's 'Materials Science' specialization list, none of them already required elsewhere in the program.

The two 'Technical Elective (at or above 300 level)' slots (Year 4 Fall and Spring) are filled with MATH461 and CHEM425, illustrative choices only -- no enumerable list of eligible technical electives exists per source, so this slot isn't audited as a program requirement.
